ENGLISH FILE
Beginner
6B  Writing
Description Students write a short text about what their hometown was like in the past
Lesson link
Use this activity after exercise 3b, page 57
Time
20 minutes
Extra material None
Instructions
a Tell SS to think about their hometown. Write on
the board: Was your hometown different when
you were a child? How? Elicit some answers and
write one or two examples on the board.
b Divide SS into pairs. Give them three minutes to
discuss the question.

While SS discuss, write on the board:
My hometown is called…
In the past there was / wasn’t…
When I was a child…
Now there is / isn’t…

Ask SS to feed back some information to the
class. Ask which grammar they used when they
talked (elicit there is / are and there was / were).
Draw SS’ attention to the useful phrases and elicit
any more that SS may want to use. Explain that
it’s useful to write down some phrases and to
consider what grammar to use before beginning
writing.
c Tell the class that they are going to do a writing
exercise. Suggest that SS work in pairs if they are
from the same town, or individually if they are
from different towns.
d Give a time limit of ten minutes and allow
dictionary use. Go around the class and help
SS where necessary. If SS are working in pairs,
encourage them to talk about their use of
grammar and vocabulary as they write.
e When SS have finished writing, ask them to read
each other’s texts. If there is time, SS could peer
correct.
